style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Split-screen isometric technical cutaway of a warehouse aisle: left half shows a building-scale automation cell with high-density pallet racking and a row of industrial robotic arms reaching toward a conveyor; right half shows a fleet of small autonomous mobile robots carrying totes along floor paths. A single corrugated cardboard case rides the central conveyor crossing the seam. Brushed steel gantries and aluminium rails sit on a polished concrete floor; palette graphite, safety yellow, bone white. A single raking key light from the upper left throws long sharp shadows to the lower right, with cool white quality. Three-quarter isometric view, unlabelled, generous negative space, no text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI elements
rationale: The story is a structural, numerical mismatch rather than a single physical product; an isometric cutaway can lay out the two pricing layers and the missing unit (the case moved) as a readable mechanical diagram without defaulting to a stock datacenter or generic robot shot.
subject: a technical isometric cutaway of a warehouse automation floor with building-scale robotic arms, a fleet of mobile robots, and a corrugated case moving on a conveyor
core_thesis: Walmart's roughly $6 billion commitment is priced per building while the industry's order index is priced per machine and excludes mobile robots, so neither number lets an operator underwrite a system against the only unit that matters: cost per case moved.
core_conflict: Building-level capex versus machine-level order index, with mobile robots omitted and no per-case handling cost disclosed.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast, three-quarter isometric view

review.depicts: An isometric cutaway view of a warehouse floor showing a tall pallet-rack structure stacked with cartons, a conveyor line fed by four yellow-and-grey articulated robotic arms (one holding a cardboard case), an overhead gantry rail, and a fleet of small white-and-yellow mobile robots carrying grey bins on a marked floor, split down the middle by a vertical line into two near-identical halves.
review.reason: It shows warehouse automation assets — robotic arms, mobile robots and a case on a conveyor — matching the story's subject of distribution-centre automation spend, though it does not itself express the per-building vs. per-machine vs. per-case cost argument.
